newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM accepts alms as monkhood nears end.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM accepts alms as monkhood nears end.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Wednesday accepted alms and prayed at a stupa in the centre of the capital Phnom Penh as part of his last full day in the monkhood.
Clad in saffron-colored robes, Ranariddh and hundreds of other monks accepted offerings of food, rice and money near the Phnom Penh railway station as hundreds of people looked on.
Ranariddh, son of King Norodom Sihanouk, is wrapping up one week of service in the monkhood according to royal family tradition.
He ends his time in the monkhood on Thursday afternoon in a ceremony at the palace.

The prince's time at Than Temple in Phnom Penh has been marked by political turmoil in the capital, as co-Premier Hun Sen threatened to call in troops and tanks to prevent the return of the king's half-brother, exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh.
Before accepting alms, Ranariddh prayed at a tree planted in 1991, when he and Hun Sen, former battlefield foes, signed the U.N.-brokered Paris Peace Accord.
The tree was sent from India as a symbol of peace in Cambodia, officials said.
